title: Fynaptix · Nuclear & SMR Research
heading: Nuclear Energy Intelligence
subheading: Small modular reactors, uranium & the AI power-demand trade
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. SMR developers are pre-revenue with long regulatory timelines; verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Expected US grid investment to match AI-driven electricity demand growth; hyperscalers hold 13+ nuclear deals totaling ~10 GW (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta). Constellation's Crane Clean Energy Center (former Three Mile Island) restart, backing a 20-year Microsoft PPA, now awaits an NRC operating-license decision targeted for May 2027, with a final NRC environmental assessment due this month

Spot holds near $90/lb while long-term contract prices hit a nominal all-time high of ~$96.50/lb this month, above the 2007 record of $95/lb; Kazatomprom's TQZ sulphuric-acid plant delay (Q3 2027-Q1 2028) continues to weigh on external reagent supply even as AI-driven demand accelerates

Constellation shares fell for six straight sessions into Sep 18 even after Q2 EPS beat estimates and management raised FY26 guidance to $11.50-$12.50/share; Morgan Stanley still lifted its price target to $369 on Sep 19 — the sell-off looks sentiment- and cash-flow-timing-driven rather than a broken thesis

Holtec Nuclear's Sep 16-18 decision to pull its ~$900M US IPO citing "market conditions" is the clearest sign yet that 2026's nuclear enthusiasm has a ceiling; NuScale's US460 remains the only SMR design with full NRC approval, and Clinch River (TVA/BWRX-300) still targets a construction-permit review decision by year-end 2026

rows.angle: Largest US nuclear fleet operator (55 GW post-Calpine); direct data-center PPAs with Microsoft, Meta, Walmart
rows.watch for: Shares fell for a sixth straight session into Sep 18, a cumulative 13% slide to ~$255, even after Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.55 beat estimates and management raised FY26 guidance to $11.50-$12.50/share (from $11.00-$12.00); Morgan Stanley nonetheless raised its price target to $369 from $364 on Sep 19. The decline is being read as investor concern over implementation and cash-flow timing rather than a break in the underlying fleet/PPA thesis

rows.angle: Major Western uranium producer + Westinghouse stake
rows.watch for: Shares fell further this week to $92.21 (day range $90.68-$96.09), extending last week's pullback; 22 covering analysts still hold an average Buy rating with a $129.23 target (+41% implied upside), and management continues to point to 77 nuclear reactors under construction worldwide plus the still-pending ~$30B Westinghouse IPO (Cameco's 49% stake) as the multi-year demand backdrop

rows.angle: Nuclear components, naval reactors, advanced reactor work
rows.watch for: Shares slid to $147.52, a new 52-week low, despite 18% revenue growth, backlog up 40% YoY and raised 2026 guidance; analyst views have diverged sharply — Guggenheim and Jefferies initiated at Buy ($192/$181 targets) while Wells Fargo stayed at just Equal Weight ($170) and Truist/Deutsche Bank trimmed targets. BWXT hosts an Investor Day on Sep 29 to make its growth case directly, on top of a new NNSA lithium-processing-facility design contract awarded Sep 2

rows.angle: Grid equipment + BWRX-300 SMR design via GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy
rows.watch for: Shares held a $926-$950 range (~$940), rising nearly 5% on Sep 16 after Blue Energy filed the initial part of its NRC construction-permit application for a Texas gas-plus-nuclear SMR plant that GEV will supply on both the gas and nuclear side; nuclear remains a small slice of GEV's overall revenue, with the ~$1,146-$1,250 median analyst target still mostly a grid/gas-equipment call

tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Fast reactors using recycled waste; Sam Altman-backed; deals directly with AI/data-center customers
rows.watch for: Shares pushed back into the high-$30s/low-$40s, closing near $40.53 on Sep 17 and touching $40.30 intraday Sep 20, as momentum continues behind Piper Sandler's Sep 10 Overweight/$55 target; Q2 revenue of $1.2M beat forecasts by over 1,000% but the net loss widened to ~$48.5M, and the ~$2B of ATM equity authorized since May remains a live dilution overhang despite the strong cash position (~$1.64B cash, minimal debt)

rows.angle: Only SMR design with NRC formal approval; utility-focused; 6-8 GW TVA/ENTRA1 partnership under discussion
rows.watch for: Shares kept sliding to the $8-9 range (from $10-11 last week), a fresh multi-week low; a Sep 15 Motley Fool piece framed NuScale as "closing in" on a transformative TVA/ENTRA1 deal, but the flagship 6GW agreement remains non-binding after more than a year of similar framing, with the CFO still targeting only a year-end 2026 resolution

rows.angle: HALEU enrichment — fuel for advanced reactors
rows.watch for: Signed a multi-year HALEU supply contract with Antares Nuclear on Sep 17, including customer prepayments that will help fund further Piketon enrichment capacity; shares rose 6.6% on the news. The deal builds on the existing $900M DOE Piketon task order and the Oklo HALEU supply agreement, and covers fuel for Antares' TRISO-fueled reactors including national-security applications

private_watchlist.name: TerraPower
private_watchlist.note: Bechtel and TerraPower split on the next construction phase of the Kemmerer Unit 1 Natrium demonstration plant (reported Sep 18-19); Bechtel filed a WARN notice for ~200 Reston, VA positions, though it says most staff will be redeployed to other nuclear projects rather than laid off, and TerraPower says the site transition is designed to protect the existing construction schedule with no anticipated changes. Separately, TerraPower's CEO told Reuters (Sep 10) that Natrium reactors could begin generating power in the UK, its first market outside the US, by 2034.

private_watchlist.name: X-energy
private_watchlist.note: Shares traded in a $15.44-$16.63 range this week. Texas Capital initiated coverage Sep 19 at Buy with a $22 target (+40% upside), directly countering Piper Sandler's Sep 8-9 Sell/$9 call from last week. Separately, UK regulators (the Office for Nuclear Regulation, Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales) formally opened a roughly three-year Generic Design Assessment of the Xe-100 reactor on Sep 15, a concrete regulatory step behind the Centrica-X-energy plan for up to 6 GW of UK capacity; DOE is also backing X-energy's Texas Xe-100 project with $1B, and the TRISO-X fuel fabrication facility (TX-1) advanced to its next construction phase.

private_watchlist.name: Kairos Power
private_watchlist.note: No new update this week. Google's first-ever corporate agreement to develop a US SMR fleet remains up to 500 MW across 6-7 units, targeting a first commercial Hermes unit by 2030 and full fleet by 2035; the Hermes 2 demonstration plant at Oak Ridge, which broke ground in April 2026, continues construction.

private_watchlist.name: Commonwealth Fusion
private_watchlist.note: The cryogenic system for the SPARC tokamak in Devens, MA reached its full 8-kelvin operating temperature this month, chilling the toroidal-field magnets colder than the surface of Pluto — a key hardware milestone ahead of the targeted 2027 scientific-breakeven (Q>1) run. Total capital raised still stands at $4B following the $1B round that closed Jul 30.

private_watchlist.name: Helion
private_watchlist.note: Helion's Polaris prototype demonstrated measurable deuterium-tritium fusion and hit a plasma temperature of 150 million°C this month, a meaningful technical milestone. OpenAI remains reportedly in talks to buy power from Helion (potentially up to 5GW by 2030) alongside the existing Microsoft PPA (50MW by 2029 via the Orion plant, under construction); no new dated news on either commercial deal this week.

private_watchlist.name: Holtec Nuclear
private_watchlist.note: Holtec suspended its planned ~$900M Nasdaq listing (ticker HNUC) on Sep 16, per Bloomberg, after targeting a $10.2B valuation just over a week earlier; Barron's called it a sign that "the nuclear euphoria of the past two years has worn off." The S-1 remains on file but no new pricing date has been set. Underlying business is unchanged: $564M trailing revenue anchored by the Palisades restart and the SMR-300 microreactor program.

bear_case.title: Holtec just pulled a $900M IPO from a company with real revenue
bear_case.description: Unlike the pre-revenue SMR developers on this page, Holtec had $564M of trailing revenue and an operating asset (Palisades) — and it still suspended its Nasdaq listing citing "market conditions" days after targeting a $10.2B valuation. If a company with an actual operating base can't get comfortable pricing conditions right now, that's a read on sector-wide investor appetite, not just one company's story.

bear_case.title: Even TerraPower's flagship project just lost its lead contractor
bear_case.description: Bechtel and TerraPower split on how to proceed with the next construction phase at Kemmerer, the most advanced private SMR project in the country. Both sides are framing it as an orderly transition with no schedule impact, but a EPC contractor walking away from the next phase of the best-funded Natrium plant is a reminder that construction execution risk doesn't disappear just because a company is well capitalized.

bear_case.title: A six-day, 13% slide in the largest nuclear fleet operator, with no bad news attached
bear_case.description: Constellation beat Q2 estimates and raised full-year guidance, yet shares fell for six consecutive sessions into Sep 18. When a name with real earnings, a raised guide, and an upgraded price target still can't hold a bid, it argues the nuclear-as-AI-power trade remains a sentiment-driven, valuation-sensitive one rather than an all-weather story.

bear_case.title: "Closing in on a deal" has described NuScale's TVA/ENTRA1 agreement for over a year
bear_case.description: Shares fell to fresh multi-week lows in the $8-9 range even as coverage continued to frame a binding 6GW PPA as imminent. The gap between narrative and a signed, binding contract is the central risk across this entire sector — a non-binding MOU is not revenue, no matter how many times it gets described as close.

catalysts.title: Holtec Nuclear pulls its ~$900M US IPO
catalysts.description: Bloomberg reported that Holtec suspended its planned Nasdaq listing (HNUC) citing market conditions, days after targeting a $10.2B valuation; the S-1 remains on file with no new pricing date set.

catalysts.title: Bechtel and TerraPower split on the next phase of the Kemmerer Natrium project
catalysts.description: The two firms could not agree on how to proceed with construction's next phase; Bechtel filed a WARN notice affecting ~200 Reston, VA roles, though it expects to redeploy most staff and TerraPower says the site schedule is unaffected.

catalysts.title: Centrus Energy signs a multi-year HALEU supply deal with Antares Nuclear
catalysts.description: The agreement includes customer prepayments to help fund further Piketon enrichment capacity and covers fuel for Antares' TRISO-fueled reactors, including national-security applications; shares rose 6.6% on the news.

catalysts.title: Blue Energy files initial NRC construction-permit application for a Texas gas-plus-nuclear SMR
catalysts.description: GE Vernova, which supplies both the gas turbines and (via GE Hitachi) the BWRX-300 nuclear-side components, rose nearly 5% on the filing progress.

catalysts.title: UK regulators open a Generic Design Assessment of X-energy's Xe-100
catalysts.description: The roughly three-year review by the Office for Nuclear Regulation, Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales follows the one-year anniversary of the Centrica-X-energy agreement targeting up to 6 GW of UK capacity.

catalysts.title: Constellation Energy falls for six straight sessions, a cumulative 13% decline
catalysts.description: The slide came despite a Q2 EPS beat and raised FY26 guidance; Morgan Stanley still lifted its price target to $369 on Sep 19, with the sell-off attributed to cash-flow-timing concerns rather than a change in the underlying fleet/PPA thesis.
